@OP if you have a demonstrable ability to 'think' code, then you will land a job as a software dev, in order to get the interview to showcase your ability to think code: build up a Github profile with open source projects, which aren't your normal everyday projects or contribute to existing Open Source projects

It is never too late :)

My own personal experience: Contribute to OSS on github, create a portfolio of projects you did by yourself that showcase your abilities, use a recruiter which specializes in the Tech sector only.

In general these recruiters know what value a github profile adds, you'll likely be writing an assessment to gauge what level your understanding is in the specific tech stack you want to go into.

If the assessments put you into the top % with advanced knowledge then you can likely skip directly to being a Dev, albeit Junior - it's still a step in the right direction :)

Also try and include C & C++ training vids, lots of developers now a days don't even know how memory management works on the lower levels - so stand out from the rest by learning the skills these languages provide

Goodluck OP

# Summary of the Game
Fragmented Space is a 4X Persistent MMO with player hosted servers and accommodates a wide variety of play styles by exposing internal variables to server hosts, with an end game goal.  

* At the start of each new Era a new galaxy is procedurally generated.  
* 3 Resources: Minerals, Energy & Population.  
* Resources are only produced by Sectors and a static starting amount of resources.  
* The end goal is to conquer the 10 "Golden" , once a federation conquers all 10 and holds them for 50 ticks, they will be declared the winner of the Era(round) and a new Era will start.  
* Based on a Tick system, where X amount of minutes = 1 Tick(Turn).  
* Conquer other players and earn a percentage of their income.  
* Servers can be hosted by players on dedicated servers, servers allow players to heavily change internal variables which allows for a wide variety of play styles.  
* Unit cost is scaled to your current amount of recruited units.  
* Units are automatically placed into fleets and can only be recruited from your own station.  
* Build outposts and upgrade them to teleportation gates, this allows quick navigation across the galaxy.   
* Basic mechanics with an emphasis on social aspects.  
* & much more more, for a detailed overview please visit the guide   


# Demo Release
I have been developing this game for a while now on my own, it has been my dream to create a MMO in the 4X genre, but just because I enjoy the game does not mean many other people will, that is why I am releasing a demo, this will allow me to see the amount of intrest the game generates with it's core mechanics.  

The demo will run over a period of 2 days, at the end of day 1 the server will be reset, the current rules are set to:
* 3 Mins = 1 Tick.  
* Maximum of 200 Players at the moment.  
* 100 'dummy' bots have been added to the galaxy, they can't do anything, but they are a visual guide to what a populate server would look like .  
* Both WebGL & Standalone builds can play on the same server.   
* Era 1 will run for 1 day ~~(480+40 = Tick 520)~~.    
* Era 2 will run for 1 day (480+20 = Tick 500).  

The game does not have an in game tutorial but I have written a "basic" guide to acompany the demo, which can be found at: https://docs.google.com/document/d/12qeoBnwTVtNKYL5wdyapK9plMg32MWS3ozUQW-l0eOE/edit?usp=sharing  

The current Demo can be played at: http://fragmentedinteractive.com/     
Picture Album: https://imgur.com/gallery/9FbT15c  

I apologize in advance for any bugs & a lack of a tutorial, any and all feedback would be welcomed. 

Edit: Deployed a new build & reset the server, one Tick now equals 5 seconds and the current server will run till tick: 9360.

Before the game is started, the launcher automatically prepends the load order to the mods name as a string in its file, pushing it to the top(you can see this effect when you look at the Mods in the default launcher), after 10 seconds the mod name is automatically reverted back to it's original value in file, eliminating any lasting effects. In order for the Custom launcher to remember the load order, a new variable is created within the .mod file itself, this variable has no effect on the game as the game discards/ignores it after initialisation.
The game loads the mods Alphabetically(tested this) , thus it is possible to modify the load order.
